title: Don't count needs-accepting re-reads toward the drain job limit
summary: When a drain re-reads an old request after a settings change and the new reading needs accepting, that attempt must not use one of the --job-limit slots, so the drain goes on to the next item. Audience: the operator running `athena drain` with a job limit and budget. The fix is in the drain's job counter, with a regression test using job limit 1.

defaults_applied.how: New regression test plus cargo test and clippy clean.
Fix the slot counting in run_job, not a special case for old requests.
The criterion runs a drain with job limit 1 and checks that the next item lands.
The check is that a batch lands the next item after a needs-accepting re-read.
Verifier runs cargo test on the drain tests.
One focused counter change with one test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs. In `run_job` (~line 1418) the order is: check stop, check `st.started >= limits.max_jobs` (JobLimit), check budget, then `st.started += 1`. It then reads or re-reads (`Source::Reread` calls `steps.reread`), then `steps.run`. `run.needs_accepting` yields `RunStep::NeedsAccepting` (~line 1537), which `attempts` maps to `ItemEnd::NeedsAccepting`, and `finish` passes the item over (~line 2411). Nothing gives the slot back, so the next item hits JobLimit. `approve_all` (~1889), `prepare` (~2008), `pick_ahead` (~2555) and the restart arithmetic (~2896) also read `st.started`. The real needs-accepting source is RealSteps::run (~line 3566). Fix: release the slot (`st.started -= 1`, saturating) when the step ends as NeedsAccepting. Money spent stays counted in the budget. The job-limit check is the one place that measures the limit.

Code survey: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. The existing `a_run_that_needs_accepting_leaves_the_item_queued_without_a_failure` (~1305) and `a_reread_whose_scope_changed_is_left_for_a_person_and_is_not_a_failure` (~2933) cover the outcome with a stub that sets `needs_accepting`. `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop` (~1422) shows how to set `max_jobs: 1`. The new test reuses that Stub pattern: item a needs accepting, item b is runnable.
No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not involved. No refusal rule is added or tightened, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.
Only the NeedsAccepting outcome releases its slot. Failed, held and passed attempts keep counting, and the job-limit stop for those is unchanged.
A change to docs or CHANGELOG is optional and not required. athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflows need no change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (Grep for `needs_accepting` near `max_jobs: 1`) drains with job limit 1 where item `a` ends as needs accepting and item `b` is runnable. It asserts `jobs[0].outcome == "needs accepting"`, `landed == 1`, and `stop != Stop::JobLimit`. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and it passes.

The same test, run against the unfixed `run_job` counter (as in the pre-change source in `git diff`), would stop with `Stop::JobLimit` before `b` runs. The assertions show it fails without the fix: `b` is asserted to land, which the old counter prevents.

`git diff` of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs shows the `RunStep::NeedsAccepting` path in `run_job` giving the started-job slot back (a decrement of `st.started` under the state lock). The JobLimit check and the other outcomes (Failed, Held, Passed) are unchanged.

A job limit that still binds for ordinary jobs: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` still passes `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop`, `an_urgent_queued_request_is_worked_before_an_approved_in_limit_proposal`, and the two existing needs-accepting tests, with no existing assertions weakened (`git diff` shows no removed asserts in them).
`cargo test` passes for the workspace and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

Doc comments or help text in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs that describe the job limit (the `--job-limit` help and the module docs near ~line 180) say a re-read that only needs accepting does not count toward it. A Grep for that wording finds it.

out_of_scope: Avoiding the re-read itself, or changing which config changes trigger a re-read.
Changing the money budget accounting; the cost of the re-read still counts against the budget.
Changing how the other outcomes (failed, held, budget short) count toward the job limit.
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted time: a batch spent all its job slots on re-reads that ended in 'needs accepting' and landed nothing.
hard_reason: It changes how the drain counts jobs against the job limit, which governs what work a batch runs or holds.
